agenda_text:
In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability-related
modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this meeting, including auxiliary aids or services,
  please call the City Clerk’s office at (818) 706-1613 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

  Any disclosable public records related to an open session item on a regular meeting agenda and
distributed by the City to the City Council less than 72 hours prior to that meeting are available for public
  inspection at City Hall (31200 Oak Crest Drive, Westlake Village) during normal business hours.

  AGENDA
  Regular Meeting of the City Council
  CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE
  City Council Chambers
  31200 Oak Crest Drive

  Wednesday, January 12, 2022 6:30 p.m.

  Written comments may be sent to the City Clerk's Office at carolk@wlv.org no later than
12:00 p.m. on Wednesday, January 12, 2022. Written comments will be summarized during the
  meeting.

Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, City Councilmembers and staff are participating in this
 meeting via teleconference pursuant to Government Code Section 54953(e). In the interest of
maintaining appropriate social distancing, a physical location is not being provided for the public
  to attend or comment. Members of the public may observe the meeting telephonically or
 otherwise electronically by using Zoom teleconference service, and may offer comment in real
  time, with the following steps:

  Please click the link below to join the webinar: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82151712300

  Webinar ID: 821 5171 2300

 Or One tap mobile : US: +16699009128,,82151712300# or +12532158782,,82151712300#
  Or Telephone: Dial(for higher quality, dial a number based on your current location):
 US: +1 669 900 9128 or +1 253 215 8782 or +1 346 248 7799 or +1 301 715 8592 or +1 312
  626 6799 or +1 646 558 8656

Teleconference participants will be muted until recognized at the appropriate time by the Mayor.
 CALL TO ORDER: 6:30 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers McSweeney, Honig, Davis, Mayor Pro Tem Pearl,
  Mayor Halpern

APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

APPROVAL OF MINUTES:  Minutes of the December 1, 2021 City Council
  Reorganization Meeting, December 8, 2021 Study
  Session Meeting, December 8, 2021 Regular City
  Council Meeting, and December 17, 2021 Special
  Session Meeting

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS/CEREMONIAL MATTERS:

PUBLIC COMMENTS: Members of the public may address the City Council on items not on the
printed agenda. Please observe the time limit of three minutes. Members of the public may offer
comment telephonically or otherwise electronically by using Zoom teleconference service options.

COUNCIL RESPONSE:

STAFF COMMENTS:

COUNCIL COMMENTS:

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS: Reports on City Council Committee meetings held.

PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  1. CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 21-008; RESOLUTION NO. 2225-22 - The City
  Council of the City of Westlake Village will conduct a public hearing to consider an application
  from Josh and Molly Breckley, on behalf of Breckley’s Bullpen, requesting approval of Conditional
  Use Permit No. 21-008, to authorize the operation of a boutique baseball and softball training
  facility, located at 31131 Via Colinas, Suites 602-604.

  2. OAK TREE PERMIT NO. 21-008; RESOLUTION NO. 2226-22 – The City Council of
  the City of Westlake Village will conduct a public hearing to consider an application from Darren
  and Miriam Goodman, requesting approval of Oak Tree Permit No. 21-008, to authorize the
  pruning of one protected coast live oak tree, located at 31552 Foxfield Drive.

  3. PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT NO. 21-006; RESOLUTION NO. 2227-22 –
  The City Council of the City of Westlake Village will conduct a public hearing to consider an
  application from Oaks Christian High School, requesting approval of Planned Development
  Permit No. 21-006, to authorize the construction of an outdoor amenity and activity space located
  at 31255 Cedar Valley Drive, for use by students at the school. The proposed outdoor space
  would be enclosed by a 10-foot landscaped wall located along the front and side property lines.
   4. ADOPTION OF NORTH BUSINESS PARK SPECIFIC PLAN COST RECOVERY
  FEES; RESOLUTION NO. 2228-22 - The City Council of the City of Westlake Village will
  conduct a public hearing to consider establishing fees for the purpose of recovering the cost to
  the City to prepare, adopt, and administer the North Business Park Specific Plan, as authorized
  by California Government Code Section 65456. The proposed fees would be levied on all new
  development within the specific plan area.

CONSENT CALENDAR: Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine
and will be enacted by one motion and one vote. Unless otherwise requested by a Councilmember, there
will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed from the
Consent Calendar and will be considered separately.

APPROVAL OF WARRANTS: Warrants effective December 15, 2021 and January 1,
2022.

  1. SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE APPROVING ZONING AND
  SUBDIVISION STANDARDS IN SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL ZONES
  RELATED TO SENATE BILL 9; ORDINANCE NO. 289-21 – Recommendation is to
  adopt Ordinance No. 289-21 titled ‘An Ordinance of the City of Westlake Village Amending
  Articles 9 and 10 of the Westlake Village Municipal Code Pertaining to Single-Family Residential
  Zoning and Subdivision Standards.’

  2. AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH R3
  CONSULTING GROUP, INC. FOR ASSISTANCE WITH SOLID WASTE
  HAULER AGREEMENT AND ORDINANCE – Recommendation is to approve an
  amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with R3 Consulting Group, Inc. dated August
  3, 2021, to increase the contract amount to $40,000 and extend the expiration date to June 30,
  2023, and that the City Manager be authorized to execute the amendment.

  3. APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. 2229-22 AUTHORIZING PROGRESS
  PAYMENTS TO LAS VIRGENES MUNICIPAL WATER DISTRICT –
  Recommendation is to adopt the attached resolution authorizing progress payments to Las
  Virgenes Municipal Water District that exceed the City’s current warrant payment limit.

  4. SUPPLEMENTAL FINDINGS FOR 2021-2029 GENERAL PLAN HOUSING
  ELEMENT; RESOLUTION NO. 2230-22 – Recommendation is to adopt Resolution No.
  2230-22 titled ‘A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Westlake Village Making
  Supplemental Findings for the 2021-2029 Housing Element’.

  5. AWARD OF CONTRACT TO RRM DESIGN GROUP FOR DESIGN OF
  WESTLAKE VILLAGE COMMUNITY PARK PICKLEBALL COURTS -
  Recommendation is to approve a Professional Services Agreement with RRM Design Group for
  the design of pickleball courts at Westlake Village Community Park.

OLD BUSINESS:

  1. APPROVAL OF THE PEDESTRIAN SAFETY STUDY FINAL REPORT –
  Recommendation is to approve the Citywide Pedestrian Safety Study Final Report.

  2. ASSEMBLY BILL (AB) 361 FINDINGS FOR SPECIAL BROWN ACT
  REQUIREMENTS FOR TELECONFERENCE MEETINGS – Recommendation is that
   the City Council make the following findings so that teleconference meetings of the City Council
  and the City’s committees can continue to be conducted pursuant to the AB 361 special Brown
  Act requirements: (1) the City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the COVID-19 state
  of emergency; and (2) state and local officials continue to recommend measures to promote
  social distancing.

  NEW BUSINESS:

  ADJOURNMENT:

To access Staff Reports go to www.wlv.org and click on City Council Agendas, Minutes & Video

MINUTES OF THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  Westlake Village, California  January 12, 2022

  CALL TO ORDER  This regular meeting of the Westlake Village City Council
  was called to order by Mayor Halpern on Wednesday,
  January 12, 2022, at 6:32 p.m., at 31200 Oak Crest Drive,
  Westlake Village, and via teleconference due to the
  ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54953(e).
  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:  Mayor Halpern led the Pledge of Allegiance.
  ROLL CALL:  Present: Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Councilmember Davis, Councilmember Honig,
  Councilmember Mcsweeney
  Absent: None

  Also Present: City Manager de Geus, City Attorney Boga,
  Deputy City Clerk Kramer, Deputy City Manager
  Eskandar, Associate Planner Sinkula, City Traffic
  Engineer Wessel
  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:  City Manager de Geus noted a change to the agenda with
  the removal of Public Hearing No. 4 to be rescheduled to
  a date uncertain. Councilmember Honig moved to approve
  the revised Agenda as presented. Councilmember
  Mcsweeney seconded the motion which carried
  unanimously.
  APPROVAL OF MINUTES :  Councilmember Mcsweeney moved to approve the
  Minutes of the December 1, 2021 Reorganization Meeting.
  Councilmember Honig seconded the motion

  YES: Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Councilmember Honig, and Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: Councilmember Davis

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed 4-yes and 1-
  Abstain (Councilmember Davis).
j
  Councilmember Honig moved to approve the Minutes of
  the December 8, 2021 Study Session Meeting, December
  8, 2021 Regular Session Meeting, and December 17,
  2021 Special Session Meeting as presented.
  Councilmember Davis seconded the motion.
   YES: Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Councilmember Davis, Councilmember Honig, and
  Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed unanimously.
 SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS/  None.
 CEREMONIAL MATTERS:

 PUBLIC COMMENTS:  Christy Vines, President, ldeos Institute, reported on their
  January 5, 2022 National Day of Dialogue event attended
  by Mayor Halpern.
 COUNCIL RESPONSE:  None.
 STAFF COMMENTS:  City Manager de Geus reported that City Hall remains
  closed to in-person visitors to keep the public and staff
  safe due to the surge in Covid-19 cases. The closure will
  be extended through January 21, 2022, at which time the
  conditions will be reassessed. Mr. de Geus stated that
  City services are still in place and managed remotely. City
  Manager de Geus commended and extended a farewell to
  Community Services Coordinator Pineda who is
  transitioning to the City of Ventura noting her last day is
  January 14, 2022. Mr. de Geus provided an update on the
  drought following the heavy rain received in the area. He
  stated that the Las Virgenes Municipal Water District did
  not end the drought emergency and reminded residents to
  continue to conserve water. City Manager de Geus
  responded to Mayor Halpern regarding the reservoir's
  percentage of capacity.
 COUNCIL COMMENTS:  Mayor Halpern reported that he attended Congresswoman
  Julia Brownley's January 6, 2022, virtual roundtable on the
  Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to discuss the Infrastructure
  Investment and Jobs Act and noted that it is the largest
  federal investment in our nation's infrastructure in
  decades. Mayor Halpern stated there will be opportunity
  for the City in areas such as broadband, transportation,
  and safety improvements.
 CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE  None.
 REPORTS:

January 12, 2022  2
  PUBLIC HEARINGS :

 CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT  City Manager de Geus introduced the item for
 NO. 21-008; RESOLUTION  consideration of a request to authorize the operation of a
 NO. 2225-22  boutique baseball and softball training facility for children
  within three units (Nos. 602, 603, and 604) located at
  31131 Via Colinas. Associate Planner Sinkula reported
  that Josh and Molly Breckley, on behalf of Breckley's
  Bullpen, requested approval to operate a training facility
  that proposes to offer three individual pitching and batting
  lanes for live hitting and pitching practice for private, one-
  on-one, and small group training classes of up to twelve
  children at a time. Mrs. Sinkula reported the proposed use
  is intended to be a private training facility for children who
  would like to improve their baseball and softball skills and
  is not intended to be a team training space. The Land Use
  Committee (Halpern/Pearl) reviewed the request on
  December 1, 2021 and recommended that it move forward
  to the City Council for public hearing.
  Associate Planner Sinkula responded to City Council
  questions regarding clarification on the number of people
  on site at any one time.

  Josh Breckley, applicant, commented on the proposed
  training facility and reasons for starting the business.

  Public Comment: Austin Harrell, Westlake Village,
  commercial real estate agent representing the Breckleys,
  commented on the service that will be provided to the
  community through the proposed business.
  Mayor Pro Tern Pearl moved that Resolution No. 2225-22,
  'A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Westlake
  Village approving Conditional Use Permit No. 21-008,
  relative to the operation of a boutique baseball and softball
  training facility located at 31131 Via Colinas, Suites Nos.
  602, 603, and 604' be adopted. Councilmember
  Mcsweeney seconded the motion.

  YES: Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Councilmember Davis, Councilmember Honig, and
  Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed unanimously.

January 12, 2022  3
  OAK TREE PERMIT NO. 21-  City Manager de Geus introduced the item for
 008; RESOLUTION NO.  consideration of a request to prune one coast live oak tree
 2226-22  located at 31552 Foxfield Drive.

  Associate Planner Sinkula provided background of the
  request where certified arborist, Christy Cuba, identified
  one protected coast live oak tree located in the rear yard
  of a residential property within the Westlake Trails
  neighborhood. The oak tree report provided a
  determination that the tree is exhibiting signs of limited
  root rot disease progression into the trunk and decay
  within an old topping cut. The oak tree report
  recommended reducing the weight of the canopy to safely
  maintain the tree. The Land Use Committee
  (Halpern/Pearl) reviewed the request on December 1,
  2021 and recommended the request move forward to the
  City Council for public hearing.
  Mrs. Sinkula responded to City Council questions and
  clarified that there were four oak trees on the property and
  that only tree number three was being discussed.
  Councilmember Honig moved that Resolution No. 2226-22,
  'A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Westlake
  Village approving Oak Tree Permit No. 21-008 to authorize
  the pruning of one protected coast live oak tree located at
  31552 Foxfield Drive' be adopted . Councilmember
  Mcsweeney seconded the motion.

  YES: Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Councilmember Davis, Councilmember Honig, and
  Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed unanimously.
 PLANNED DEVELOPMENT  Planning Director Forbes presented a request to authorize
 PERMIT NO. 21-006;  the construction of an outdoor amenity and activity space
 RESOLUTION NO. 2227-22 for use by students at Oaks Christian School, 31255
  Cedarvalley Drive, located in the North Business Park
  Specific Plan (NBPSP) area. Mr. Forbes provided
  background of the proposed project stating the proposed
  outdoor space, formerly a parking lot, would be screened
  by a 10-foot landscaped wall located along the front and
  side property lines. The proposed space would include
  amenities such as shaded outdoor study areas, water

January 12, 2022  4
   features, an outdoor kitchen with a barbeque and eating
  areas, and a sports court.

  Mr. Forbes noted the applicant requested exceptions to
  two development standards related to setbacks and height
  of the wall:

  1. Front and side yard setbacks - Req uired:
  minimum 10-feet. Requested: No setbacks for wall.
  Purpose: Zero setback requested to maximize use
  of outdoor space; landscaping will provide
  appearance of setback.

  2. Maximum wall height- Required: maximum 42
  inches within front setback; maximum six-feet
  elsewhere. Requested: 10 feet.
  Purpose: 10-foot wall requested to provide student
  privacy and security.

  Planning Director Forbes explained that the NBPSP
  allows exceptions to be granted through the Planned
  Development Permit (PDP) process rather than a
  variance.

  Planning Director Forbes provided an overview of the wall
  and the extensive landscaping proposed for the screening
  of the wall. Mr. Forbes explained that there is no sidewalk,
  the entire area is landscaped, and the wall would be fully
  covered with vegetation.

  On December 1, 2021, the application was reviewed by
  the Land Use Committee (Halpern/Pearl) and
  recommended it move forward to the City Council.
  Mike Parkinson, applicant, and Planning Director Forbes
  responded to City Council questions regarding: 1. Gate
  material, and 2. Dormitory building occupancy.

  Councilmembers commented on Oaks Christian's
  responsiveness, willingness to compromise, provisions of
  landscaping, and gate design.
  Councilmember Davis moved for adoption of Resolution
  No. 2227-22, titled 'A Resolution of the City Council of the
  City of Westlake Village Approving Planned Development
  Permit No. 21-006 Authorizing Construction of an Outdoor
  Amenity and Activity Space at 31255 Cedarvalley Drive.
  Councilmember Honig seconded the motion.

January 12, 2022  5
   YES: Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Councilmember Davis, Councilmember Honig, and
  Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed unanimously.
 CONSENT CALENDAR:  Councilmember Mcsweeney moved to approve the
  Consent Calendar. Councilmember Honig seconded the
  motion.

  YES: Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Councilmember Davis, Councilmember Honig, and
  Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed unanimously.

  APPROVAL OF WARRANTS: Warrants effective
  December 15, 2021 in the amount of $531,418.22, and
  January 1, 2022 in the amount of $204,887.59.

  GENERAL BUSINESS:

  1. Second Reading of Ordinance Approving Zoning
  and Subdivision Standards in Single-Family
  Residential Zones Related to Senate Bill 9;
  Ordinance No. 289-21 - Recommendation was to
  adopt Ordinance No. 289-21 titled 'An Ordinance of
  the City of Westlake Village Amending Articles 9
  and 10 of the Westlake Village Municipal Code
  Pertaining to Single-Family Residential Zoning and
  Subdivision Standards.'

  2. Amendment to Professional Services Agreement
  with R3 Consulting Group, Inc. for Assistance with
  Solid Waste Hauler Agreement and Ordinance -
  Recommendation was to approve an amendment
  to the Professional Services Agreement with R3
  Consulting Group, Inc. dated August 3, 2021, to
  increase the contract amount to $40,000 and
  extend the expiration date to June 30, 2023, and

January 12, 2022  6
   that the City Manager be authorized to execute the
  amendment.

  3. Approval of Resolution No. 2229-22 Authorizing
  Progress Payments to Las Virgenes Municipal
  Water District - Recommendation was to adopt the
  attached resolution authorizing progress payments
  to Las Virgenes Municipal Water District that
  exceed the City's current warrant payment limit.

  4. Supplemental Findings for 2021-2029 General Plan
  Housing Element: Resolution No. 2230-22 -
  Recommendation was to adopt Resolution No.
  2230-22 titled 'A Resolution of the City Council of
  the City of Westlake.Village Making Supplemental
  Findings for the 2021-2029 Housing Element'.

  5. Award of Contract to RRM Design Group for
  Design of Westlake Village Community Park
  Pickleball Courts - Recommendation was to
  approve a Professional Services Agreement with
  RRM Design Group for the design of pickleball
  courts at Westlake Village Community Park.
 OLD BUSINESS:

 APPROVAL OF THE  City Manager de Geus introduced the item and provided a
 PEDESTRIAN SAFETY  historical perspective of the citywide pedestrian safety
 STUDY FINAL REPORT  study report and the recommendations. He thanked the
  Public Safety Advisory Board for their time commitment,
  perspectives, and efforts throughout the process. He also
  thanked City Traffic Engineer Mark Wessel for his project
  management work. Mr. de Geus noted that the Pedestrian
  Safety Study will serve as a reference document to the
  City Council and staff as annual goals, budgets, and
  capital improvement plans are developed.

  City Traffic Engineer Wessel presented a short summary
  of the Citywide Pedestrian Safety Study Final Report. Mr.
  Wessel reviewed the Recommendations Summary
  identifying the priority under each major toolbox category:

  1. Education - Pedestrian Education,
  2. Engineering - Building Sidewalks, and
  3. Enforcement - Speed, Yielding, Distraction, and
  DUI.

January 12, 2022  7
   Mr. Wessel concluded that final decisions will be made
  during the upcoming goals meeting and budget process.

  Councilmember Honig moved to approve the Pedestrian
  Safety Study Final Report as presented. Mayor Pro Tern
  Pearl seconded the motion.

  YES: Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Councilmember Davis, Councilmember Honig, and
  Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed unanimously.
  ASSEMBLY BILL (AB) 361  City Manager de Geus introduced the item and provided
7  FINDINGS FOR SPECIAL  an overview of Assembly Bill (AB) 361 addressing findings
  BROWN ACT  that must be made for the City to continue teleconference
  REQUIREMENTS FOR  meetings pursuant to special Brown Act requirements.
  TELECONFERENCE  Staff's recommendation was that the City Council make
  MEETINGS  the AB 361 findings so that the City will continue to have
  greater flexibility to conduct teleconference meetings
  during the COVID-19 state of emergency.
  Mr. de Geus stated that on December 8, 2021, the City
  Council discussed returning to in-person meetings at
  which time it was the consensus of the City Council to
  continue with teleconference meetings for the January 12,
  2022 meeting and evaluate conditions further. With the
  high rate of COVID-19 infections in Los Angeles County,
  staff recommended that the City Council continue to use
  the teleconference option for City Council meetings
  through February 9, 2022, and at that time, discuss a
  timeline for returning to in-person meetings.
  Mayor Pro Tern Pearl moved that the City Council make
  the following findings so that teleconference meetings of
  the City Council and the City's committees can continue to
  be conducted pursuant to the AB 361 special Brown Act
  requirements: (1) the City Council has reconsidered the
  circumstances of the COVID-19 state of emergency; and
  (2) state and local officials continue to recommend
  measures to promote social distancing. Councilmember
  Mcsweeney seconded the motion.

  January 12, 2022  8
   YES: Mayor Halpern, Mayor Pro Tern Pearl,
  Councilmember Davis, Councilmember Honig, and
  Councilmember Mcsweeney.
  NO: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed unanimously.
 NEW BUSINESS:  None.
 ADJOURNMENT:  The meeting was adjourned at 7:28 p.m.

  On behalf of the City Council and staff, Mayor Halpern
  thanked Community Services Coordinator Taylor Pineda
  for her service and wished her all the best and good luck
  in her future role.

  Brad Halpern, Mayor
